structure.note: 537,582,089 listed 'A' shares (par CHF 1.00) and 537,582,089 unlisted 'B' shares (par CHF 0.10). Each share has one vote, and each share's portion of net profit and liquidation proceeds is in proportion to its par value, so a 'B' share receives one-tenth of the dividend of an 'A' share. All 'B' shares are held by Compagnie Financière Rupert, which also holds 6,418,850 'A' shares: 10.18% of the capital and 50.60% of the voting rights. The directors regard Compagnie Financière Rupert as the Group's controlling party. The only other holder above 3% at 31 March 2026 was UBS Fund Management (Switzerland) AG, with 32,456,632 shares or 3.02% of the voting rights.

notes: Fiscal year ended 31 March 2026 (FY2026, matching data.js 'Mar 2026'); all figures from the Richemont Annual Report and Accounts 2026 on richemont.com. Reported in EUR, converted exactly from € millions. OWNERSHIP: Johann Rupert holds his interest through Compagnie Financière Rupert (CFR), of which he is the General Managing Partner (Chairman of Richemont); Anton Rupert, a non-executive director, is also a partner. The report does not say how CFR's own equity is split among its partners, so the stake is recorded in family (labelled as CFR) and leader.pctEconomic is null. The 10.18% is CFR's share of the Company's capital (par value), which is also the basis for profit and liquidation entitlements. Voting control is 50.60% (stated precisely this year; the FY2025 report said 'some 51%'). 'Parties associated with Mr Johann Rupert and Compagnie Financière Rupert held a further 2 921 335 'A' shares'; their % of capital is not stated, so it is not added. relation 'founder': his board biography states 'He founded Richemont in 1988'. HOLDERS: the only other disclosed holder above 3% is UBS Fund Management (Switzerland) AG with 3.02% of the voting rights; the report gives no percentage of capital for it, so it is named in the structure note rather than listed. BUYBACKS: 0 under the site's rule that purchases covering employee plans are not cash returned to shareholders. The cash-flow statement shows 'Acquisition of treasury shares' of €186m (1.1 million shares), which note 30.2 says hedges obligations under share-based compensation plans; proceeds from treasury share sales were €30m. There was no buyback programme for cancellation. To count the gross purchases instead, use 0.19. DIVIDENDS: €1,888m to owners of the parent (plus €1m to non-controlling interests, excluded). STOCK COMP: €116m equity-settled share-based compensation expense. GEOGRAPHY: from FY2026 the note presents five main areas (Japan is now shown separately from Asia Pacific); the note also gives country detail (e.g. United States €4,875m, mainland China €2,656m). In January 2026 Richemont agreed to sell Baume & Mercier to the Damiani Group; YNAP's sale to Mytheresa (now LuxExperience) completed on 23 April 2025.
